text: {"distance_m": 0.9, "reasoning_short": "Rough estimate (±50%) from Blackwell-type threshold data plus Ricco's law, not an exact limit. 20/20 acuity (1 arcmin) applies to high-contrast detail, so it does not set the limit for a 5%-contrast spot. For small spots, the contrast needed to see them rises as size shrinks, roughly with contrast × area held constant. At indoor light levels, 5% contrast becomes detectable once the spot spans about 4 arcmin (≈0.0012 rad). A 1 mm spot subtends that angle at about 1 mm / 0.0012 ≈ 0.85 m, so roughly 0.9 m."}
